item.title: Episode 29: Hijacked GitHub accounts plant a CI secret stealer, ScreenConnect panels push rogue clients and new N-central exploits beat the hotfix, 13 November 2026
item.description: An attacker used 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts to plant a CI secret stealer that ran in at least 1,835 repositories, and attackers with access to cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels pushed rogue clients to at least 288 endpoints across 48 organisations. New N-central exploit chains work against this week's hotfix where the Legacy API is exposed, and the Bookeasy booking breach now affects national parks customers in Queensland, Victoria and South Australia. Global threats Hijacked GitHub accounts plant CI secret stealer (from 10 November 2026). Aikido: 4,837 accounts, test pull requests in 61,764 repositories, stealer ran in at least 1,835 and credentials exfiltrated (an earlier Aikido figure was 1,806); SafeDep: 8,093 public repositories received malicious commits (7,309 workflow edits, 771 npm postinstall hooks). Steals Actions secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN, OIDC tokens, cloud and AI keys; exchanges OIDC for AWS/GCP/Azure sessions; persistence via AWS role trust policy rewrite and Entra federated credentials named wfx-ci-* . Overlaps with October GhostAction accounts; not attributed to the same actor. Indicators: PR title docs: dependency audit notes ; branches wfx-docs , chore/[a-z0-9]{8} , ci-check-[0-9]{4} ; commits ci: refresh build cache , chore: add ci helper , chore: add dependency audit workflow , ci: restore , ci: cleanup ; stealer SHA-256 89695abb392d5cfd4972672961e644bb46baa98aa1ed7173c2a2816c762735cf ; exfil 194.150.166[.]244:8080 , 18.143.168[.]96:8080 , 153.75.82[.]159:8080 , plus Telegram. Malicious packages: Packagist digitalelvis/neuronai-studio 3.14.3 (pin 3.14.2 or earlier); Go github.com/onuragtas/docker-env v1.0.278 and v1.0.280 (workflow file only); github.com/vkuznet/gocurl v0.0.0-20261111095532-8d5aad0cb0da. Aikido ; SafeDep ; The Hacker News ScreenConnect panels used to push rogue clients and SCKit (first detected 11 November 2026, 17:47 UTC). Huntress: at least 288 endpoints across 48 organisations that use Huntress (a floor); Huntress update (11 November, 11:34pm ET) links access to the third-party RMM+ extension, versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, which accepted a blank access key when none was configured, bypassing ScreenConnect accounts, roles and MFA; payload designed to spread endpoint to technician to panel (onward spread not yet observed). ConnectWise disabled Labtech Plus, RMM Plus, RMM+, RMM Plus Password Link and RMM+ Password Link extensions; no evidence of ConnectWise infrastructure compromise or a flaw in ScreenConnect; ConnectWise had not confirmed an initial access vector. Blackpoint: SCKit attempts a Guest-to-Host technique associated with the already patched CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9); in its lab test a current Host client did not request or run the payload. Indicators (ConnectWise): 185.99.255[.]28 , 155.94.150[.]39 , ns[.]mo7sen[.]dev , sc[.]payproofkit[.]com , cdn007-digitaldownloads[.]com , newnewnew[.]gotdns[.]org , Soxnewwork[.]homedns[.]org ; artefacts sckit-run.bat, sckit-decoder.ps1, TrapWatch.ps1, Panel-Lateral.ps1, Run-Lateral-Full.bat, ToolboxRelayUploader.exe. ConnectWise advisories ; Huntress ; Blackpoint Cyber ; Sophos ; The Hacker News N-central: 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell exploits work against 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (12 November 2026). Researcher claims unauthenticated root RCE on the server (4EverAble2Shell, documented by Previdian against build 2026.4.1.26) and SYSTEM command execution on Windows agents (Agent2Shell, needs the appliance ID; not independently verified). Previdian notes the full affected range and a fixed build are unverified. Affected: on-premises N-central 2026.4.1 HF2 (build 2026.4.1.26) with Legacy API enabled and internet-exposed; hosted not affected. Disable Legacy API. Previdian recorded 2 exploitation attempts from 1 IP ( 157.20.241[.]16 ) on 12 November, chaining Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436; attempts only, no successful exploitation reported. N-able advisory wording via The Hacker News. N-able status ; Previdian ; The Hacker News Red Hat Quay key-server flaw (CVE-2026-123710, CVSS 9.8) and robot token leak (CVE-2026-110697, CVSS 9.9). All Quay 3 and Quay 5 versions listed as affected; fixed builds for eight Quay 3 branches; Quay.io fixed. Block /keys at the proxy, audit service_key_rotate and service_key_delete events with null expiry, remove unknown keys, then update. Red Hat CVE-2026-123710 ; Red Hat CVE-2026-110697 ; Red Hat remediation Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 RCE (CVE-2026-119618, CVSS 9.8). Affected: 2.4.55 to 2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled; standalone mod_h2 2.0.8 to 2.0.42 (no fixed release). Apache advisory ; Red Hat ; Wiz Citrix patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client flaws. ABC News ; 7NEWS ; Sydney Morning Herald VCAA: VCE exams go ahead after website hack (12 November 2026). ABC News AI security TypoPrompting: 186 lookalike domains for 27 AI brands (Island). Routes to ClickFix PowerShell lures, the Microsoft Store-signed Net Guard app with hidden browser control, and 16 search-hijack Chrome extensions (about 972,000 declared users as of 3 November 2026). Island ; The Hacker News BluePhishing: consent phishing for Microsoft Entra Agent ID blueprints (Proofpoint, 9 November 2026). Victims approve a malicious agent blueprint, creating an attacker agent identity in their tenant. Microsoft Message Center MC1506733: default Entra users can create agent blueprints by default from November 2026. Proofpoint Industry and patches Node.js fixes 16 flaws, including HTTP/2 crash CVE-2026-123863 and memory leak CVE-2026-123866. Fixed: 22.23.5, 24.22.3, 26.13.1. The Hacker News MongoDB pre-authentication crash on failover (CVE-2026-118383). Datadog Security Labs reproduced it. The Hacker News PTC Windchill and FlexPLM deserialisation RCE (CVE-2026-126325, CVSS v4 9.2). CVE record lists specific affected releases from 11.0 M030 to 13.1.4.0 for Windchill, and similar for FlexPLM. The Hacker News Google Cloud: AMD Turin TSA side channels (CVE-2024-36350, CVE-2024-36357, CVE-2026-0004). C4D, N4D, H4D, Z4D and G4 VMs need a guest OS patch and a stop and start. item.title: Episode 28: Barracuda email gateways exploited, Railway's stolen AI keys cost 740,000 dollars and the VCAA website hacked mid-exams, 12 November 2026
item.description: Attackers are exploiting two Barracuda flaws that chain to root on Email Security Gateway appliances, and CISA has given US federal agencies until 13 November to act. Railway's incident report puts unauthorised AI usage from keys stolen in its October breach at an estimated US$740,000, and the VCAA website was hacked during Victoria's exam period. Microsoft Research showed a model backdoor made by editing fewer than ten neurons. Global threats Barracuda authorisation bypass and command injection exploited (CVE-2026-116606, CVSS 9.3; CVE-2026-111560, CVSS 8.6). Bypass needs no login, but the Admin UI must be reachable (ESG only; Barracuda revised this wording on 5 November); command injection needs administrative access and affects ESG, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, WAF and Web Security Gateway; chained from an exposed Admin UI, they give root. Barracuda (update 9 November 2026 EST) reports exploitation affecting a small number of organisations. Added to CISA KEV 10 November 2026, forensic triage required, federal due date 13 November 2026. Patches: ESG BNSF-40425 (firmware 9.4.017 and later) or BNSF-40430 (earlier than 9.4.017); ADC and WAF BNADC-16586; BMA BNMA-32468; WCC BNWF-60060; WSG BNYF-24789. Restrict Admin UI to trusted internal networks. KEV references Mandiant advisories MNDT-2026-0041 and MNDT-2026-0042. Barracuda advisory ; CISA KEV N-able N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 released (update to Able2Shell, 10 November 2026, US time). Build 2026.4.1.26 fixes CVE-2026-125883, CVE-2026-125881, CVE-2026-125878, CVE-2026-125879, CVE-2026-125882, CVE-2026-91000 and CVE-2026-125880; affected: versions before 2026.4.1. Hosted servers upgraded; on-premises servers stay offline until upgraded; upgrade Agents before Probes; built-in remote control temporarily disabled; a further hotfix is planned. Scanning reported, no confirmed customer compromise. Tenable FAQ ; BleepingComputer ; Infosecurity Cisco BroadWorks XXE (CVE-2026-20320, CVSS 7.5) and Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder (CVE-2026-111793) added to KEV (10 November 2026). BroadWorks: unauthenticated read of configuration files; advisory first published 19 August 2026; fixed from release RI.2026.07; no workarounds. Openwave: an authenticated attacker uploading a crafted file may obtain sensitive information; fixed in Webtop Media Transcoder 1.1.22.0 (JVN published 9 November 2026, rated Critical; developer reports observed attacks). Federal due date 24 November 2026. Cisco advisory ; JVN JVNVU#93403064 ; Openwave advisory ; SecurityWeek Zoom Workplace for Windows privilege escalation (CVE-2026-108186, CVSS 9.6; CVE-2026-108187, CVSS 8.1). Not reported exploited. CVE-2026-108186 (ZSB-26023) is network-reachable without authentication but requires user interaction. Affected: CVE-2026-108186, 7.1.0 to before 7.1.8; CVE-2026-108187, before 7.1.5. Fixed: 7.1.8 or later. Zoom ZSB-26023 ; The Hacker News Git recursive-clone code execution (CVE-2026-111760). Index path-length integer truncation lets a malicious repository redirect a submodule's .git to attacker hooks; requires cloning with --recurse-submodules. Fixed (10 November 2026): 2.56.1, with 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1 and 2.55.1. Git for Windows had no 2.56.1-based release as of 10 November 19:09 UTC (per The Hacker News). GitHub Blog ; oss-security eMudhra revokes eight more intermediate CAs (7 November 2026). RSA intermediates (six TLS, two other) revoked because eMudhra cannot show compliant key handling by the script behind its October compromise; keys not shown to be weak. Mozilla Bugzilla 2083449 ; The Hacker News Australian focus VCAA website hacked during Victoria's exam period (11 November 2026). VCAA is running a forensic investigation and says there is no indication exam papers were accessed. The attacker's claims (papers taken from a printing provider's file servers and sold to students; email details from a legal services provider) are unverified. Exams run to 18 November. ABC News Parks Victoria pauses new campsite bookings after Bookeasy breach (11 November 2026). Suspicious WhatsApp messages sent to customers; Parks Victoria does not use WhatsApp. Existing bookings remain valid. Parks Victoria via Mirage News AI security Railway incident report: stolen AI keys, about US$740,000 unauthorised usage (10 November 2026). Build-infrastructure flaw, over-trusted build credential, misconfigured identity binding, then a decryption credential; variables decrypted in at most 1.85% of workspaces (about 100,000); linked-account tokens for 1,852 users reset. Railway will cover charges providers don't refund. Railway incident report ; iTnews Microsoft Research "Lazarus": backdooring agents by editing fewer than ten dormant neurons. In recorded tests with a harmless marker command, seven edited neurons in Nemotron-Terminal-8B emitted it on at least 98.8% of held-out trigger runs and on no benign runs (in free generation, one setup emitted it in 0.14% of no-trigger sessions, per The Hacker News); rates measure command emission, not completed attacks; requires write access to weights; Microsoft says not seen in use (per The Hacker News). Microsoft Research ; Microsoft Security Blog ; The Hacker News AntiFox agentic pentest platform used in IIS and AWS intrusions (Arctic Wolf, 10 November 2026). Alibaba Cloud-hosted instances. One pattern: ASPX web shells, web.config credential harvesting, wide AWS enumeration, one successful GetSecretValue on a production secret. Other cases began with valid AWS credentials obtained by unknown means; one involved S3 reads, copies and deletes. BleepingComputer ; The Hacker News Claroc: 35,578 of 37,571 online Grok app addresses found via passive DNS open without sign-in (10 November 2026). Claroc tried 43,551 addresses, of which 37,571 were still online. "Anyone with the link" was preselected in the account tested; about one in ten held business or personal data; 24 staff apps from SpaceXSI and X taken down. Claroc NEAR AI breached through SGLang RCE (disclosed 9 November 2026). Code ran on one TEE-hosted inference server; on 8 November the attacker could have observed requests processed on that server, including confidential ones; account details of about 100 users and data from 18 legacy agents accessed; two Cloud customers' API keys exposed in logs and revoked (company figures). NEAR AI incident report Patch priorities Critical: Barracuda ESG and appliances (exploited); N-able N-central on-premises (Hotfix 2 before reconnecting). High: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave (exploited); Zoom Workplace for Windows; Git on build systems. Watch: VCAA investigation; Bookeasy breach scope; further N-central hotfix.

item.title: Episode 26: Attacker rides Qubole's trusted AWS access, GPUStack and FreeSWITCH flaws exploited and a German host breached through its MCP server, 10 November 2026
item.description: An attacker used credentials for Qubole's AWS account to assume the integration roles customers had created for the data platform, then took secrets and S3 data, mostly through roles that showed no other legitimate vendor use that month. CISA added three actively exploited flaws to its KEV catalogue: GPUStack, FreeSWITCH and the OpenSSH *sshole bypass, where researchers now report post-exploitation activity. Vanderbilt University is responding to an active cyber incident, German host Mittwald was breached through its MCP server, and Victorian medical group Epichealth disclosed unauthorised access affecting patient information. Global threats Qubole cross-account trust abused in customer AWS environments (Wiz, with Sentra and Mandiant, 9 November 2026). Between 14 and 26 October 2026 an attacker used IAM credentials from AWS account 805246085872 (used by Qubole's platform) to AssumeRole into customer integration roles; every request carried a valid External ID and succeeded. Enumeration, Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store and Lambda environment variables harvested; TruffleHog used to validate discovered AWS, Entra ID and Okta credentials; S3 exfiltration, sometimes entire buckets. Most abused roles showed no other legitimate vendor AssumeRole activity in October. How the credentials were obtained has not been disclosed. A separate 8 to 11 October set of activity used customer-owned access keys created for Qubole integrations. Hunt from 1 October 2026 for AssumeRole events from 805246085872 from non-AWS addresses, principal IDs AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS and AIDAJYRRH5Y3A7AAJM2HW, and session names starting quiam- . Mitigations: remove unused vendor trust, pin trusted principal and add aws:SourceIp or aws:SourceVpce conditions, treat External ID as non-secret, enable S3 data events. Wiz ; The Hacker News CISA adds three exploited flaws to KEV (9 November 2026, due 12 November 2026 for covered US federal civilian agencies). CVE-2026-102895 (GPUStack, see AI security), CVE-2026-123158 (OpenSSH *sshole) and CVE-2026-116779 (SignalWire FreeSWITCH). CISA KEV * OpenSSH sshole update (CVE-2026-123158). Now in CISA KEV. GreyNoise observed successful exploitation followed by reconnaissance, attempts to read password hashes and root SSH keys, authorized_keys changes and a command-and-control implant; the attempted credential reads are not confirmed as successful. Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 (restart sshd), or set PasswordAuthentication no. Background in Episodes 23 and 25. GreyNoise ; BleepingComputer FreeSWITCH SIP MESSAGE command execution (CVE-2026-116779, CVSS 9.8). An accepted inbound SIP MESSAGE can select the api chat protocol and run FreeSWITCH API commands, including OS commands, as the FreeSWITCH process; stock profiles accept MESSAGE. SignalWire says exploitation has been observed in the wild. Affected: all releases up to and including 1.11.2. Fixed: 1.11.3 (adds enable-chat-api-proto , off by default). Workaround: enable-chat=false on profiles that don't need chat; make sure every directory user has a password (this reduces exposure but does not close the path for a valid account). FreeSWITCH advisory ; Ostorlab analysis ; Rescana Vanderbilt University active cyber incident (9 November 2026, US time). Incident may affect university devices, systems and cloud services. University asked its community to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. BYOD ransomware group listed the university and claims student and employee data (unverified). Vanderbilt ; The Record Ethersphere bee-js and Swarm Desktop compromised (9 November 2026). Malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 published through the project's release automation; steal the Swarm Desktop wallet key and password and install a backdoor on Windows, macOS and Linux. Withdrawn; Swarm Desktop 0.56.3 replaces the compromised 0.56.2; researchers recommend rolling back to bee-js 13.2.0 (a pre-incident release). Treat hosts that installed the bad versions as compromised; move funds to a new wallet and rotate secrets from a clean machine. Swarm Desktop release ; bee-js 13.2.0 ; The Hacker News ; Ostorlab LNbits tells all operators to shut down servers (8 November 2026). Wave of attacks; one operator reports 2,285,545 satoshis (about 0.023 BTC) withdrawn by new accounts. Developer estimated a fix within 24 to 48 hours on 8 November (upper end about 1am AEDT Wednesday 11 November); the release page still listed 1.6.2 as latest at last check. Watch for an official fixed release and restart guidance. The Hacker News ; LNbits releases Bitter deploys PapRAT in South Asia (Fortinet FortiGuard Labs, 2 November 2026). New RAT in C++ and Rust; delivery via LNK abusing ftp.exe and VHDX images with lure spreadsheets. Fortinet Australian focus Epichealth Medical Clinic cyber incident (notice dated 4 November 2026). Four Victorian clinics (Warrnambool Medicare Urgent Care Clinic, Ocean Grove Marketplace, Ocean Plaza, Portarlington). Information that may be affected: name, date of birth, contact details, Medicare card number, Centrelink CRN, DVA number and health information. Reported to ACSC and OAIC; clinics open. Separately, Cyber Daily reports The Gentlemen listed Epichealth on 31 October; the notice does not attribute the incident or confirm theft. Epichealth notice ; Cyber Daily ANZ implementing an enterprise AI control plane (FY26 results, 9 November 2026). Planned centralised visibility, governance and technical control across users, models, agents, tools, costs and platforms, with traceability and limits on agent activity. Underlying software not disclosed. iTnews ; ANZ BlueNotes AI security GPUStack authentication bypass exploited (CVE-2026-102895, CVSS 9.8). Before the fix, a request appearing to come from loopback was treated as the built-in administrator when force_auth_localhost was false (the default), reachable via a same-host reverse proxy or a forged X-GPUStack-Real-IP header. The flaw lets attackers create persistent admin API keys and read worker and cloud-provider secrets; the vendor reports an exploited 2.1.1 deployment where custom inference backends ran reverse shells. Affected: versions before 2.2.0. Fixed: 2.2.0. Workaround: force_auth_localhost=true and strip client-supplied X-GPUStack-Real-IP . Review users, API keys and backends; rotate worker and cloud secrets. GitHub advisory ; Ostorlab Mittwald breached through its MCP server (disclosed 7 November 2026). Flaw first tested 21 October, exploited 27 October, detected 4 November; 56 customer projects compromised; MCP server shut down. Mittwald cites speed of activity as indicating AI tool use, with no other evidence offered; unclear whether the flaw was in its own code or open-source libraries. Mittwald (German) ; The Record BOSSAI: one attacker, twelve configured AI agents, nine active (Acronis TRU, 4 November 2026). Attacker placed in Hualien City, Taiwan; hundreds of targets in at least 11 countries; about 10 accessed in Taiwan, Mexico and Thailand, including Taipei 119 dispatch case records from seven districts. Attack agents ran mostly on locally hosted models with safety training removed after commercial models refused; a scanner invented CVEs and more than half of its high and critical findings were false; in the observed attacks, agents failed where logins were enforced. Acronis ; The Hacker News Industry and research PwnEscape (CVE-2026-99999) turned into a Firecracker escape (pwn.ai, part 2 published 9 November 2026). Host-kernel IPv4 virtio-net/TAP checksum flaw; demonstration used Firecracker v1.16.1 run as root without the jailer. AWS: EC2, Lambda and Fargate not affected. Affected kernels: 4.4 through 6.18 per AWS. AWS bulletin Upstream fix commit 6785011f8b16; patch the host kernel and reboot. Kernel CVE team score 9.3; Red Hat, Amazon and SUSE 8.8. iTnews ; pwn.ai Outlook and patch priorities Critical: GPUStack 2.2.0 plus key and backend review; FreeSWITCH 1.11.3 or enable-chat=false ; OpenSSH 10.6p2 plus checks for planted keys and services. High: audit cross-account IAM trust (Qubole customers first); host kernel patch and reboot for self-run KVM/Firecracker; LNbits offline until fixed. Watch: Microsoft November Patch Tuesday (early Wednesday 11 November, Melbourne time); BYOD claims on Vanderbilt; Mittwald's detailed account.

item.title: Episode 17, Sunday Special: Australia's Cyber Threat Report 2025-26, 1 November 2026
item.description: ASD's seventh Annual Cyber Threat Report, released this week, says AI has amplified and sped up existing threats rather than creating new ones. This Sunday Special draws out five messages: patch in days, attackers log in rather than break in, medium businesses are taking the biggest cost rise, incidents are up and more serious, and the answer is an assumed-breach mindset plus the basics, with a short look at critical infrastructure. The report ASD's ACSC Annual Cyber Threat Report 2025-26. The full report, including the "assumed breach" call and the Essentials series. https://www.cyber.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/Annual%20Cyber%20Threat%20Report%202025-26.pdf ASD release. https://www.asd.gov.au/news/2026-10-27-australian-signals-directorate-releases-seventh-annual-cyber-threat-report-2025-26 Last year's report (2024-25 summary), for comparison. https://www.cyber.gov.au/about-us/view-all-content/reports-and-statistics/annual-cyber-threat-report-2024-2025 business.gov.au summary for businesses. https://business.gov.au/news/annual-cyber-threat-report-2025-26 Key figures (not read on air) ASD changed how it categorises incidents in 2025-26, so category comparisons with 2024-25 are not like for like. - More than 82,000 cybercrime reports to ReportCyber, about one every six minutes, down about 3% from 84,700. - 1,524 incidents responded to, up from 1,253 (ASD says "more than 20%"). - More than 4,400 notifications to entities, up almost 80% by ASD's comparison. This year's total includes collective notices (about 2,200 individual notifications, up 33%, plus collective notices to about 2,100 entities). - Hotline calls: 37,500, down 12%. - Extensive compromises: 40, from 26 (not like for like); extensive ransomware incidents 24, from 16; extensive DDoS (distributed denial of service) 7, from 1, while overall DoS and DDoS incidents fell more than 60% to 80+. - Ransomware steady at 139 incidents. - Data breach incidents: 98, up 66%, about 6% of incidents (as a share, data breaches have stayed steady: 7% in 2021-22, 6% now). - Published CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) up 30%. - ASD tip-offs led to 362 incidents being found; one cPanel notification to 340 entities led to 60+ confirmed incidents. - Health Care is now the top non-government reporting sector (7%). Manufacturing entered the top 10 and Transport left it. - Average self-reported cost per business report: $93,500, up 16% (from $80,850). Small $55,400 (about flat, from $56,600). Medium $141,300, up 45% from $97,200. Large $148,100, down 27% from $202,700, partly reversing last year's 219% rise. - Individuals: $33,000 average per report, unchanged (separate from the "overall" average of $38,130). - 55% of people reuse passwords (Act Now. Stay Secure. campaign research quoted in the report). - Some exploitation occurs within 48 hours of a patch or mitigation advice; most within two weeks. A flaw from 2008 was exploited successfully this year. Critical infrastructure What the report says. Critical infrastructure (CI) is an attractive target for extortion because of its sensitive data and critical services; ASD says state-sponsored actors "routinely target" Australian CI networks, possibly for espionage or to pre-position against operational technology (OT) in a crisis or conflict. https://www.cyber.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/Annual%20Cyber%20Threat%20Report%202025-26.pdf Figures. 154 CI incidents, 10% of all incidents (similar to last year), down almost 7%; category changes mean this is not like for like. Top ways in: phishing 36%, valid accounts 16%, drive-by compromise 10%. Top sectors: Financial and Insurance Services 30%, Public Administration and Safety 21%, Electricity, Gas, Water and Waste Services 17%. OT and supply chain examples. Pro-Russia hacktivists reached OT through exposed VNC remote access (ASD and partners advisory, 10 December 2025). An Iranian group's claimed compromise of Stryker, a US-based company that imports surgical and pharmaceutical equipment into Australia, was a supply-chain exposure rather than a direct attack. Guidance. ASD's CI Fortify guidance for operators is on cyber.gov.au. Outside the report: ASD interviews this week Amadey botnet disruption and stolen-data destruction (ABC). ASD disconnected one Amadey botnet from about 180,000 infected computers worldwide. In a separate operation it destroyed 5 TB of stolen data, including about 4.8 million files from Australians. https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-27/australian-signals-directorate-ai-cybersecurity-hacking-threats/107309858 ABC AM interview. Includes ASD's comments on future disruption and incident-response protocols with frontier AI labs. https://www.abc.net.au/listen/programs/am/asd-warns-of-looming-cyber-disruptions/107312354 ESET tracks 53 Amadey botnets (The Hacker News). https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/australia-gets-into-amadey-malware.html AI on offence: confirmed versus claimed Anthropic's exploit chains (lab work, not attacks). Five chains (Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, Linux); fixes confirmed and credited; "little human involvement" is Anthropic's own account; none seen in real attacks. https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/anthropics-unreleased-ai-model-chains.html PHP2Shell intrusions (Dream's assessment). 25 servers rooted according to Dream, three in a US government-affiliated environment; nearly 40 scripts judged AI-assisted; Dream says it has "no direct evidence" AI wrote the exploit. https://dreamgroup.com/blog/chained-php2shell-exploit-roots-25-servers ; https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/php2shell-attack-roots-25-servers.html ARTEX, South Korea (police allegations). Seven suspects, more than 90 organisations, about 8.2 million records, 360 million won demanded in 38 incidents; not tested in court. https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/former-pentester-used-artex-ai-to-steal-82-million-data-records/ Warp (company disclosure). Agent logs and telemetry exposed via a third-party vendor, "roughly 1%" of users; the "agent swarm" description is the CEO's account only. https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/warp-discloses-breach-exposing-ai-agent-logs-user-telemetry-data/ What to do Report cybercrime at https://www.cyber.gov.au or on 1300 CYBER1 (1300 292 371).

  • ASD release. https://www.asd.gov.au/news/2026-10-27-australian-signals-directorate-releases-seventh-annual-cyber-threat-report-2025-26
  • Last year's report (2024-25 summary), for comparison. https://www.cyber.gov.au/about-us/view-all-content/reports-and-statistics/annual-cyber-threat-report-2024-2025
  • business.gov.au summary for businesses. https://business.gov.au/news/annual-cyber-threat-report-2025-26

Key figures (not read on air)

ASD changed how it categorises incidents in 2025-26, so category comparisons with 2024-25 are not like for like. - More than 82,000 cybercrime reports to ReportCyber, about one every six minutes, down about 3% from 84,700. - 1,524 incidents responded to, up from 1,253 (ASD says "more than 20%"). - More than 4,400 notifications to entities, up almost 80% by ASD's comparison. Medium $141,300, up 45% from $97,200. Large $148,100, down 27% from $202,700, partly reversing last year's 219% rise. - Individuals: $33,000 average per report, unchanged (separate from the "overall" average of $38,130). - 55% of people reuse passwords (Act Now. Stay Secure. campaign research quoted in the report). - Some exploitation occurs within 48 hours of a patch or mitigation advice; most within two weeks. A flaw from 2008 was exploited successfully this year.

Critical infrastructure

  • What the report says. Critical infrastructure (CI) is an attractive target for extortion because of its sensitive data and critical services; ASD says state-sponsored actors "routinely target" Australian CI networks, possibly for espionage or to pre-position against operational technology (OT) in a crisis or conflict. https://www.cyber.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/Annual%20Cyber%20Threat%20Report%202025-26.pdf
  • Figures. 154 CI incidents, 10% of all incidents (similar to last year), down almost 7%; category changes mean this is not like for like. Top ways in: phishing 36%, valid accounts 16%, drive-by compromise 10%. Top sectors: Financial and Insurance Services 30%, Public Administration and Safety 21%, Electricity, Gas, Water and Waste Services 17%.
  • OT and supply chain examples. Pro-Russia hacktivists reached OT through exposed VNC remote access (ASD and partners advisory, 10 December 2025). An Iranian group's claimed compromise of Stryker, a US-based company that imports surgical and pharmaceutical equipment into Australia, was a supply-chain exposure rather than a direct attack.
  • Guidance. ASD's CI Fortify guidance for operators is on cyber.gov.au.

Outside the report: ASD interviews this week

  • ESET tracks 53 Amadey botnets (The Hacker News). https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/australia-gets-into-amadey-malware.html
